newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas up ahead of Taiwan tender.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas up ahead of Taiwan tender.

text.p: Gasoline extended its gains in a well-bid market ahead for Taiwan's reformate import tender which closes Tuesday, traders said on Monday.
"There are a lot of bids ... everybody wants it up," said a trader.
Traders said bids for 95-octane unleaded cargoes were raised by 10 cents from Friday's level to $25.35 per barrel. The bid for 92-octane was similalry raised to $25.00.
Taiwan, which usually buys at a fixed price, is seeking 250,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate for delivery March 1-15 to Keelung or Taichung.
"Everyone is looking towards Taiwan for indicative levels," said a trader.
Some traders assessed fundamentals to be balanced to tight on the back of reductions in reformer and refinery througputs.
A source at the 285,000 barrel-per-day Singapore Refining Co said it had cut some 40,000-bpd of output January 23-February 3. Two other refiners have already cut production by some 90,000-bpd.

As a result, the India buy tender was awarded at almost $5.00 over Singapore 92-octane unleaded quotes, higher than a similar cargo for February 8-12 which was awarded in the last tender at a premium of $2.50 over 92-octane unleaded quotes.
The latest tender, for 25,000 tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline cost-and-freight Goa/Kandla February 15-29, was awarded to BP.
IOC has another gasoline tender for February 21-25 delivery to the same ports which closes January 29, and is valid until January 31.
Naphtha was lacklustre and prices moved down with crude. February swaps fell by around 20 cents to $23.20/$23.40.
